BACKGROUND

On January 13, 2021, the City authorized a construction services contract for the installation of water and wastewater main improvements at 12 locations and water transmission main valve improvements at 27 locations. The construction contract included air release valve improvements on the 90-inch and 84-inch diameter White Rock North Water Transmission Main. This critical pipeline moves up to 190 million gallons of water per day to customers in North Dallas, East Dallas and customer cities. Sudden disruptions in pump operation, such as would result from a power outage, can cause pressure surges which could rupture the pipeline. A pipeline rupture would cause property damage and disruption in service to water customers. The air release valve improvements will reduce the risk of pipe rupture from surge events and should be completed as soon as possible to protect this critical pipeline.

This action will authorize an increase in the contract with John Burns Construction Company of Texas, LLC for additional work associated with air release valve improvements to the White Rock North Transmission Main system. The work was originally part of another construction contract that included installation and replacement of various air release valves. However, the contractor had several payment disputes with subcontractors, submitted unreasonable payment claims, and unilaterally demobilized from the site without completing the entire work. Despite exhaustive efforts to work with the contractor and surety company, neither has upheld their contractual obligation to complete the work ultimately prompting the City to terminate the original contract.

The work includes five 18-inch diameter taps, one 8-inch air release valve installation, and eight 6-inch air release valve installations on water transmission main infrastructure. Additionally, the contractor will finish associated items left incomplete by the previous contractor and surface restoration of sites with previous activity by the original contractor.

SUBJECT

..Title

*In alignment with Economic Development Incentive Policy.

..Body
BACKGROUND

Chapter 372 of the Texas Local Government Code ("Act") allows for the creation of public improvement districts ("PIDs"). The RedBird Public Improvement District ("District") was created by the City Council on May 28, 2025 in accordance with the Act by Resolution No. 25-0872. On August 27, 2025, by Resolution No. 25-1408, the City Council designated Red Bird Public Improvement District Inc. ("RBPIDI") as the manager of the District and authorized a management agreement with RBPIDI to be funded from special assessments on taxable property in the District.

In addition to that ongoing management agreement funded from special assessments on taxable property in the District, this agreement now before City Council is a separate and distinct agreement with RBPIDI and is proposed to be funded solely by a discretionary allocation of City Council District 3 ARPA Redevelopment Fund dollars. Unlike the management agreement authorized by City Council on August 27, 2025 (which governs the District's long-term management beginning January 1, 2026), this management agreement now before City Council will provide one-time stand-alone support to ensure the District has the organizational capacity and resources necessary to launch operations during its first year (i.e., prior to the receipt of special assessment revenues). This management agreement does not amend, replace, or duplicate the management agreement authorized by City Council on August 27, 2025, and this management agreement creates no future fiscal year commitments.

RBPIDI shall enhance the PID's operational and community impact during the District's first year of operation by providing: 

* Strategic planning, legal framework, accounting system/infrastructure, and other organizational development services, including engagement of professional consultants to prepare a multi-year, strategic business plan to guide the District's operations
* Safety and security initiatives including installation of surveillance cameras across high-priority areas of the District, establishment of a centralized command center in the District, and development of an annual security plan
* Beautification and wayfinding improvements, including design and fabrication of directional signage, commissioning of community-based artwork in collaboration with local artists and stakeholders, and implementation of a five-year beautification plan with identified phases, budget projections, and maintenance protocols 
* Branding, marketing and promotional efforts, specifically development of a marketing and communications plan inclusive of a district website, logo, informational materials, and stakeholder engagement collateral
* Other supplemental services and improvements that provide a public benefit and support the mission of the District

The term of the management agreement is anticipated to begin on or after December 1, 2025 and terminate on December 31, 2026.

Pursuant to Texas Local Government Code Chapter 252.022(7), this management agreement is exempt from the bidding requirements because the management services are available from only one source. Specifically, the petition establishing the District designated RBPIDI as the management entity, as authorized by Chapter 372 of the Texas Local Government Code, and City Council confirmed and authorized this designation by Resolution No. 25-1408 on August 27, 2025.

PRIOR ACTION/REVIEW (COUNCIL, BOARDS, COMMISSIONS)

On February 28, 2024, the City Council authorized the transfer and reallocation of ARPA funds from the U.S. Department of Treasury for the Coronavirus Local Fiscal Recovery Fund to the ARPA Redevelopment multi-year fund to provide assistance with completing projects by Resolution No. 24-0315.

On May 28, 2025, the City Council authorized the creation of the RedBird Public Improvement District for a period of ten years by Resolution No. 25-0872. 

On August 27, 2025, the City Council designated Red Bird Public Improvement District Inc. as the manager of the District, authorized a management agreement funded from special assessments on taxable property in the District, and approved the District's 2026 Service Plan, by Resolution No. 25-1408.

The Economic Development Committee was briefed by memorandum regarding this matter on October 6, 2025.

These items are only available from Northern Air Systems, Inc. and not through any distribution or reseller network.

Northern Air worked with and successfully tested units to accommodate DAS and its DAL tenants, showing that their design, performance and technologies are unique/superior to other units currently offered in the marketplace.

..Body
BACKGROUND

This action does not encumber funds. The purpose of a service price agreement is to establish firm pricing for services, for a specific term, which are ordered on an as needed basis according to annual budgetary appropriations. The estimated amount is intended as guidance rather than a cap on spending under the agreement, so that actual need combined with the amount budgeted will determine the amount spent under this agreement.

This service agreement will provide managed services supporting the Software as a Service UMAX billing system for the Dallas Water Utilities Department. Managed services will include product level support, security event monitoring and handling, release management and deployment, non-break-fix support, product training, and batch and interface monitoring. The integrated billing system produces approximately 20,000 documents daily, ranging from invoices and past due notices to service requests, permit renewals, consumer applications, and fee statements.  It bills more than $575 million in utilities revenue and over $1 billion annually for other departments' revenue.

In 2006, the City of Dallas secured Axon to implement SAP, a highly customized billing system. Axon was transitioned to Deloitte providing managed services for the SAP System. SAP processes became too complicated and caused upgrade issues due to customizations. The system required special skill sets to manage the system due to custom-made coding language.






On May 8, 2024, the City Council approved a ten-year service contract for a citywide integrated customer information and billing software system for the Dallas Water Utilities Department with Itineris NA, Inc. The initial Itineris NA, Inc. contract provides implementation services for the UMAX Customer Information System and SaaS software licensing. 

UMAX is built for utilities. Processes are configured out of the box instead of developed. Maintenance and configuration of the system will be easier to manage by the city staff. Itineris provides Saas ready maintenance and support services on the software. 

The functionality of the UMAX system includes:

* Monthly billing for water, wastewater, sanitation, and stormwater service fees
* Capture, dispatch, and/or resolution of all water and wastewater customer service requests
* Participating departments' collection activities for delinquent receivables
* Monthly contractual billing for aviation landing and baggage fees, and cashiering for security badges
* Permit applications/renewals and fees for other departments
* Fees for high-risk fire inspection, and lien/loan statements

The integrated billing system is a mission critical system used 24 hours a day making it essential that a maintenance and support agreement be in place for timely and technical responses should unplanned malfunction or service disruptions occur.  This service agreement will also provide periodic software upgrades, system patches and non-break-fix solutions.

BACKGROUND

This service contract agreement will authorize a contract for the deployment of 100 Artificial Intelligence (AI) -enabled data collection units to enhance operational efficiency and service delivery for the Department of Sanitation Services (SAN), in partnership with the Department of Code Compliance (CCS).

This contract will provide the purchase, installation, training, and support of camera technology mounted on 50 Sanitation brush and bulky waste collection trucks, with cameras positioned on both sides to capture curbside property conditions as part of regular collection routes.

This innovative technology will allow SAN to collect data on customer participation in brush and bulky item collection services, which vary by season and location, enabling staff to better align equipment and resources across the city, promote more efficient service delivery, reduce unnecessary mileage, and support long-term rate stability for customers.

In partnership with CCS, the system will also provide automated, citywide visual scans approximately every 30 days, producing real-time, actionable data on conditions such as illegal dumping, graffiti, and structural deterioration. These insights will allow CCS staff to shift from reactive enforcement and complaint-based inspections toward proactive identification of community needs, improving response times and resource deployment.







Beyond sanitation and code enforcement benefits, the platform supports data-informed planning, neighborhood outreach, and grant reporting, helping the City achieve a more efficient, service-first approach to community maintenance and education. Funding for this contract was approved by the City Council as part of the FY 2024-25 budget adoption in September 2025.

Key benefits:

* Automated Data Collection and Analysis 
* Customizable Reporting and Analytics Dashboard
* Training and Ongoing Support for City Staff 
* Enhanced Grant Application Support

BACKGROUND

On December 11, 2024, the City Council approved an increase in the total city direct cost share under the Project Partnership Agreement with the United States (U.S.)  Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) to complete design and construction for the Modified Dallas Floodway Project Flood Risk Management Project, which includes Charlie 2 Pump Station. USACE awarded a design-build contract in March 2022 and finalized construction plans in December 2023. USACE authorized the contractor to proceed with construction in April 2024.  

The project will protect nearby properties from frequent flooding and reduce the risk of loss of life. The Charlie 2 Pump Station is designed to collect and pump up to 225,000 gallons per minute (gpm) of stormwater over the West Levee into the Trinity River Floodway. Pump station capacity includes three 75,000 gpm concrete volute pumps and one 6,000 gpm low flow sump pump. Construction is ongoing as of Winter 2025 and is anticipated to be completed in Winter 2026. 

This action will authorize a Facilities Extension Agreement with Oncor Electric Delivery Company, LLC to provide permanent electrical service to the pump station and ensure the facility can operate as designed to deliver reliable flood protection to the surrounding area.

On December 11, 2024, the City Council authorized an increase in the total city direct cost share for the Project Partnership Agreement (PPA) with the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (Corps) to complete design and construction for the Modified Dallas Floodway Project Flood Risk Management Projects by, Resolution No. 24-1746.

*In alignment with Infrastructure Management Plan. 

..Body
BACKGROUND

This action does not encumber funds; the purpose of these agreements is to establish firm pricing for services and goods, for a specific term, which are ordered on an as needed basis according to annual budgetary appropriations. The estimated amounts are intended as guidance rather than a cap on spending under the agreement, so that actual need combined with the amount budgeted will determine the amount spent under these agreements.

These agreements will provide actuator repair services and the purchase of butterfly valves, parts, and actuators for the Dallas Water Utilities Department.  Butterfly valves are used to control the flow of water within water treatment facilities. Services provided for the actuators shall include troubleshooting, removal, installation, repairs on failed equipment, or the replacement thereof.



The master agreement will provide replacement valves, plant control process valves, and valves for new installation of water transmission lines for water treatment plants. Certain valves will be used to isolate sections of the water/wastewater system to allow repairs to existing water mains and to permit additional construction. Butterfly valves range in size from 6" to 96" with the larger valves requiring additional production time. In some applications butterfly valves need to be electronically automated remotely, therefore, an actuator is attached.  

The Dallas Water Utilities Department distributes an average of 400 million gallons of treated water and 160 million gallons of wastewater daily.  

As part of the solicitation process and in an effort to increase competition, the Office of Procurement Services used its procurement system to send out email notifications to vendors registered under relevant commodity codes.  To further increase competition, the Office of Procurement Services uses historical solicitation information, the Internet, and vendor contact information obtained from user departments to contact additional vendors.

On November 10, 2015, the City Council authorized a living wage policy that requires contractors to pay their employees a "living wage" rate as established annually by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology Living Wage Calculator for Dallas County by Resolution No. 15-2141. The calculated living wage during the solicitation process of this contract is $22.05; the selected vendors meet this requirement.

On May 25, 2022, the City Council authorized (1) a three-year service price agreement for the maintenance and repair of butterfly valve actuators for the Water Utilities Department with Machining and Valve Automation dba MVA Services, Inc. and (2) a three-year master agreement for the purchase of butterfly valves, parts and actuators for the Water Utilities Department with Municipal Valve & Equipment Company, Inc, Mueller Co., LLC and Macaulay Controls Company by Resolution No. 22-0808.

BACKGROUND

Dallas Water Utilities Department's (DWU) Stormwater Operations is responsible for the maintenance and operation of the City's drainage system. To accommodate the Dallas Area Rapid Transit (DART) Silver Line, Hillcrest Road was lowered and the Hillcrest Pump Station was constructed to provide flood mitigation and enhance public safety associated with these public improvements. The proposed project includes an enclosure that will support Stormwater Operations by protecting critical drainage infrastructure and mitigating environmental impacts, including visual and noise effects, associated with the City's stormwater pump station. Jacobs Engineering Group, the project's retained consultant engineer, designed a house-like enclosure to surround the existing pump station equipment and reflect the architectural character of the adjacent residential area.

This action will authorize a construction services contract with Big Sky Construction Company, Inc. for the construction of the Hillcrest Road Pump Station House Project enclosure. The site is located at 17404 Hillcrest Road at the corner of Hillcrest Road and McCallum Boulevard across from the Northeast Dallas Police Substation.  The construction is to be funded by the North Central Texas Council of Governments (NCTCOG) with a total available construction budget of $1.8M. 

Big Sky Construction Company, Inc. has had no contractual activities with the City of Dallas for the past three years.

*In alignment with Water and Wastewater Capital Improvement Program. 

..Body
BACKGROUND

The Dallas Water Utilities Department (DWU) owns and operates numerous pieces of operational equipment critical to the distribution and metering of water and collection of wastewater. On September 11, 2019, the City Council authorized a professional services contract with Espey Consultants, Inc. dba RPS Infrastrucuture, Inc. for engineering and architectural services for the design, construction administration, and start-up associated with the Large Valve and Meter Project. A condition assessment of various DWU owned meters and meter vaults was performed to identify and prioritize improvements to extend their service life, reduce operational and maintenance costs, and improve worker safety. Improvements to this infrastructure will help ensure DWU continues to meet production demands, accurately monitors wastewater flows for treatment, and meets environmental regulations mandated by the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality.

Engineering designs and specifications were prepared for the improvement of large valves and meter vaults at 15 locations. On June 25, 2025, a construction services contract for the Large Valve and Meter Vault Project was awarded to John Burns Construction Company of Texas, LLC. The project includes the replacement of large-diameter butterfly and gate valves, rehabilitation or reconstruction of deteriorated meter vault structures, modifications to valve chambers for safe access and fall-protection compliance, improvements to appurtenance, drainage, bypass piping, and site restoration, coordination for shutdowns, maintenance of operations, and impacts to adjacent utilities, and traffic control and permitting for vaults located within public rights-of-way (ROW).

This action authorizes Supplemental Agreement No. 1 to the professional services contract with RPS Infrastrucutre, Inc. to provide additional construction phase services for the Large Valve and Meter Vault Project at fifteen locations. The additional services include project partnering, monthly construction meetings and periodic site visits, additional submittal reviews, coordination with operations and review of contractor tie-in plans, monthly construction schedule and pay application reviews, review of operation and maintenance manuals, start-up support and record drawing services, and project closeout and final inspection services. Completion of the project will improve the water and wastewater system resiliency, reduce emergency repair response, enhance public safety, and maintain accurate wholesale metering.

Began Design	October 2019
Completed Design	January 2025
Began Construction	January 2026
Construction Completion	September 2028

SUBJECT

..Title
A resolution authorizing the (1) acquisition of an easement from Oncor Electric Delivery Company, LLC; and (2) conveyance of an easement and right-of-way containing, a total of approximately 2,240 square feet of land to Oncor Electric Delivery Company, LLC for the construction, maintenance and use of power lines and electric transformer facilities across City-owned land located near the intersection of Mountain Creek Parkway and Clark Road - Financing: No cost consideration to the City 

*In alignment with Water and Wastewater Capital Improvement Program. 

..Body
BACKGROUND

This item authorizes the conveyance of an easement and right-of-way containing, a total of approximately 2,240 square feet of land to Oncor Electric Delivery Company, LLC for the construction, maintenance and use of power lines and electric transformer facilities across City-owned land located near the intersection of Mountain Creek Parkway and Clark Road. DWU has identified the need for water transmission pipeline improvements through the Water Distribution Master Plan and Long-Range Water Supply Plan to facilitate conveyance of treated water to the South and Southwest portions of Dallas and its customer cities. The proposed easement and right-of-way conveyance will allow Oncor Electric Delivery Company, LLC to relocate its infrastructure being displaced due to the construction of a portion of the Southwest Pipeline Water Transmission Project. 

The Southwest Pipeline Water Transmission Project includes the installation of approximately 32 miles of 96-inch and 120-inch diameter water transmission pipeline to meet demands associated with population growth as determined through master planning efforts. The overall pipeline is sized to meet future water demands and will be completed in multiple phases based on funding availability and timing need for additional water capacity. When completed, the pipeline will provide additional system capacity, redundancy, and resiliency. This easement and right-of-way conveyance is necessary to complete the first phase which includes the construction of approximately 26,900 feet of 96-inch diameter pipeline from the Summit Ground Storage Tanks in Cedar Hill southeast to Wintergreen Road, then east along Wintergreen Road to Old Hickory Trail in DeSoto.

This item, on behalf of Dallas Water Utilities Department, authorizes the conveyance of an easement and right-of-way containing a total of approximately 2,240 square feet of land to Oncor Electric Delivery Company, LLC for the construction, maintenance and use of power lines and electric transformer facilities across City-owned land located at the intersection of Mountain Creek Parkway and Clark Road.

This easement will facilitate the relocation of existing electric lines and associated infrastructure being displaced due to the construction of a portion of the Southwest 120/96-inch Water Transmission Pipeline Project parcel W-121. Future electrical infrastructure relocation costs will be required.

This item has no prior action.

No cost consideration to the City.

This item authorizes the conveyance of an easement and right-of-way containing, a total of approximately 2,098 square feet of land to Oncor Electric Delivery Company, LLC for the construction, maintenance and use of power lines and electric transformer facilities across City-owned land located near the intersection of Bank Street and Herndon Drive in Dallas, Texas. DWU is currently constructing the Mill Creek/Peaks Branch/East Peak Branch Drainage Relief Tunnel, which includes the construction of a dewatering pump station on City of Dallas owned property near the intersection of Bank Street and Herndon Drive. The proposed action will convey an easement and right-of-way to Oncor to facilitate the installation of an electrical transformer needed to serve the dewatering pump station associated with the Mill Creek/Peaks Branch/East Peak Branch Drainage Relief Tunnel.

The Mill Creek/Peaks Branch/East Peaks Branch Drainage Relief Project includes a five-mile drainage tunnel to reduce recurring flooding and improve stormwater infrastructure in some of the city's most flood-prone urban neighborhoods. When completed, it will provide significant flood relief south of the tunnel and to areas immediately along the alignment including Baylor Hospital, south of Buckner Park, Fair Park, and State-Thomas near Woodall Rodgers. Part of the project includes a pump station that will be used when the tunnel needs to be dewatered for inspection and maintenance.

..Title
A resolution authorizing the conveyance of an easement and right-of-way containing, a total of approximately 831 square feet of land to Oncor Electric Delivery Company, LLC for the construction, maintenance and use of power lines and electric transformer facilities across City-owned land located at 12000 Greenville Avenue - Financing: No cost consideration to the City 

*In alignment with Water and Wastewater Capital Improvement Program.

..Body
BACKGROUND

This item authorizes the conveyance of an easement and right-of-way containing, a total of approximately 831 square feet of land to Oncor Electric Delivery Company, LLC for the construction, maintenance and use of power lines and electric transformer facilities across City-owned land located at 12000 Greenville Avenue. Dallas Water Utilities Department (DWU) is currently constructing a new Service Center that includes a 26,260 square foot, 2-story concrete tilt-up panel building on approximately 12.9 acres. The building will be a key operational facility for DWU and electrical service and transformer connections are necessary to complete the project.

Construction of the new facility is approximately 70 percent complete, with completion anticipated by Fall 2026. The new DWU Service Center will consolidate Wastewater Emergency Response and Stormwater Neighborhood Drainage Services currently operating out of temporary and leased facilities into a single permanent location. Approval of this item, including conveyance of the required easement to Oncor, is necessary to allow installation of an electrical transformer and associated electrical infrastructure. Conveying the easement is critical to establishing permanent power to the facility and avoiding delays to the project's scheduled completion.

This item has no prior action.

Street outreach staff are essential to the encampment decommissioning and re-housing process, and are responsible for delivering the following services: (1) engagement with people experiencing unsheltered homelessness, (2) conducting coordinated access system assessments, (3) service coordination and connection to community-based resources, (4) housing navigation to support people on a pathway to permanent housing, and (5) data entry and reporting to monitor performance.

On January 24, 2024, the City Council authorized a twenty-month contract with Housing Forward as a sole source, for outreach services enhancing the efforts of the Real Time Rehousing Project formerly Dallas Real Time Rapid Rehousing (DRTRR) by Resolution No. 24-0180.

On September 17, 2025, the contract term was extended until March 31, 2026, an additional six months, through the Office of Procurement Services by Extension Request Letter 25-1148. 

On March 31, 2026, Administration Action No. 26-5524 authorized Supplemental Agreement No. 1 that extended the contract term until May 31, 2026, and added additional funds in the amount of $220,000.00.

..Title
Authorize a professional services contract with Kimley-Horn and Associates, Inc. to provide engineering services associated with the assessment and preliminary design of improvements for the Sorcey Pump Station and major maintenance improvements at Dallas Water Utilities Department's water distribution facilities - Not to exceed $3,290,060.00 - Financing: Water Capital Improvement G Fund

*In alignment with Water and Wastewater Capital Improvement Program.

..Body
BACKGROUND

The Dallas Water Utilities Department (DWU) provides treated drinking water and fire protection to approximately 2.65 million people through an extensive water delivery system. DWU's water distribution infrastructure includes numerous potable water pump stations and pumps, water storage tanks, pressure reducing valves, and more than 5,000 miles of transmission and distribution mains. As these facilities age and system demands increase, DWU must continue to plan, prioritize, and implement strategic major maintenance improvements to ensure reliability, regulatory compliance, and operational efficiency across the water delivery network.  

This action will authorize a professional services contract with Kimley-Horn and Associates, Inc. to provide engineering services associated with the assessment and preliminary design of improvements for the Sorcey Pump Station and major maintenance improvements at 22 additional water distribution facilities. The engineer will prepare a 30 percent preliminary design assessment for high-priority major maintenance improvements across these facilities, including Sorcey Pump Station, 19 additional pump stations, and three elevated storage tanks. The project will document existing conditions, evaluate facility needs, develop preliminary design concepts and cost estimates, and produce a ranked list of construction projects aligned with DWU's operational goals, long-term planning, and budget constraints. Detailed engineering design, bidding, and construction phase services will be authorized under a future supplemental agreement after completion of the assessment and preliminary design. 

Completion of this assessment and preliminary design effort will provide DWU with a clear data-driven plan for near-term major maintenance investments that enhance system reliability, improve operability, and reduce life-cycle risks across critical distribution facilities.

Complete Services		July 2027

BACKGROUND

This action does not encumber funds; the purpose of a service contract is to establish firm pricing for services, for a specific term, which are ordered on an as needed basis.

This service contract will provide for a subscription-based records system for pawned and second-hand property transactions, as well as investigative software services for the Dallas Police Department. The system for pawned and second-hand property transactions will enable the Police Department's Fusion Center to search nationwide pawnshop and second-hand store records as part of criminal investigations.  This system provides information about the property being sold and links the seller.  All pawn shops are required, by the State of Texas, to report all property transactions to local law enforcement.

The additional investigative tools included in this contract support critical law enforcement functions, such as data analysis, investigative research, cellular mapping, and information sharing across cases.

Previously, these services were maintained under multiple agreements, which created administrative inefficiencies and fragmented workflows. This contract consolidates these services into a single agreement, improving operational efficiency, enhancing data integration, and ensuring continuity of service. 



LeadsOnline, LLC is the sole source provider of this integrated system. The platform includes proprietary technology and exclusive access to a nationwide database of transaction records and investigative tools that cannot be replicated by other vendors.

Additionally, services will be provided in English, Spanish, and other languages through a nationwide network of International Board-Certified Lactation Consultants.

The Supplier provides detailed call data for program evaluation that has demonstrated a significant increase in breastfeeding rates.

*In alignment with Water and Wastewater Capital Improvement Program.

..Body
BACKGROUND

The Iron Bridge Pump Station (IBPS), located at 4777 County Road 3706 in Wills Point, Texas 75169, is a critical asset for the Dallas Water Utilities Department (DWU) that pumps raw water from Lake Tawakoni to the Tawakoni Balancing Reservoir for storage before flowing via gravity to the East Side Water Treatment Plant for treatment. The IBPS is one of three raw water pump stations in DWU's eastern water supply system, with Lake Tawakoni being the oldest of the three eastern system reservoirs.

The IBPS was constructed in the 1960s and has been in service for over 55 years and is due for near-term rehabilitation to maximize its useful life. Much of the equipment and pump station components in the station date back to the original construction and are inefficient and expensive to operate and potentially dangerous to maintain. There are numerous hydraulic, structural, electrical, architectural, and other needs that require attention to ensure the continued reliable operation of the pump station.

In 2010, an engineering assessment and preliminary design were completed to rehabilitate and expand the capacity of the IBPS. The project was delayed in 2012 due to a need to keep IBPS in operation as the Lake Fork Pump Station was being commissioned. Improvements of IBPS faced further delays due to budget constraints until 2021, when an assessment of the pump station was finalized to develop scope for a near-term project including rehabilitation and repairs in lieu of a major pump station expansion.

This action will authorize a construction services contract with Walsh Construction Company II, LLC dba Archer Western, for DWU's Iron Bridge Pump Station Rehabilitation Project. The project improvements consist of lake bank reinforcement, site access gate replacement, structural repairs throughout the pump station, including concrete, flumes, guard rails, and upper-level rehabilitation, roof replacement, elevator rehabilitation, louvers and door improvements. In addition, construction services will also include process-mechanical items such as intake gates and actuator improvements, bridge crane improvements, pump discharge valving, surge control automation, demolition of existing hydraulic system, pump, motor, base frame leveling and miscellaneous improvements, electrical rehabilitation related to low-voltage equipment, medium-voltage equipment, new electrical feed to process-mechanical equipment, backup generator and lighting; and related instrumentation and control improvements.

*In alignment with Water and Wastewater Capital Improvement Program.

..Body
BACKGROUND

The Dallas Water Utilities Department (DWU) owns and operates an existing 60-inch diameter reinforced concrete wastewater main that was constructed in the 1950’s and is in poor structural condition.  Given the flow carried by the existing wastewater main and existing condition, it has a high likelihood and consequence of failure and requires rehabilitation to improve its condition and extend its useful life. Rehabilitation of the existing main was identified as part of larger improvements recommended in DWU’s 2020 Comprehensive Wastewater Collection System Assessment Update. 

Due to environmental and easement constraints and the existing pipe’s deteriorated condition, it was determined that the best course of action would be to first renew the existing pipe via rehabilitation to address the high risk and consequence of pipe failure. Pipeline renewal will enable more time for comprehensive planning, design, land acquisition, and construction of a larger capacity relief main. This action will authorize a construction service contract for the rehabilitation of approximately 5,150 linear feet of existing 60-inch diameter wastewater main. Approximately 4,790 linear feet will be rehabilitated by Machine Spiral Wound Liner and approximately 360 linear feet will be rehabilitated using Cured-In-Place-Pipe followed by High-Density Polyethylene slip lining for the portion of the pipeline crossing the Trinity River. 




Proposals were received from the Request for Competitive Sealed Proposal  procurement process and were evaluated based on published criteria which include proposed contract price, schedule, contractor’s approach to the project, experience and past performance of the contractor, experience and qualifications of key personnel, and Developing Regional & Inclusive Vendor Enterprise policy requirements. The proposals were evaluated and scored by a selection committee and Ruby Collins, Inc., was determined to be the best value proposer based on the rating criteria.

Ruby Collins, Inc. has had no contractual activities with the City of Dallas within the past three years.
